verdict.rationale: Aider's own docs cover headless operation: the `--message` flag runs one natural-language instruction, applies the edits and exits, and a Python scripting API (`Coder.create`/`coder.run`) runs an instruction and returns. Command-line switches, `.aider.conf.yml` and `AIDER_xxx` environment variables make it configurable for automated pipelines, and `--test-cmd`/`--auto-test` can run tests after each edit. Missing for 10: a documented CI pipeline guide or example (e.g. a GitHub Actions recipe), documented non-interactive confirmation and exit-code behavior for CI, and independent hands-on reports of CI use (the one community comment only says they 'should consider' scripting).

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can run the product headlessly / in CI for automation

citations.quote: Aider takes a `--message` argument, where you can give it a natural language instruction. It will do that one thing, apply the edits to the files and then exit.
aider --message "make a script that prints hello" hello.js
# This will execute one instruction on those files and then return
Or by setting environment variables like `AIDER_xxx`
You can configure aider to run your test suite after each time the AI edits your code using the --test-cmd <test-command> and --auto-test switch.
